In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
access rural banking = re vo mi
access growth credit = pa to mi
rural growth savings = vo lu to
banking credit savings = lu pa re
access rural savings = lu mi vo
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: to. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: access = mi, rural = vo, banking = re, growth = to, credit = pa, savings = lu.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 28 km east, turns right and walks 30 km, then turns right and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 34. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 16 km along the initial direction and 30 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(16² + 30²) = 34 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 140 km north, turns left and walks 240 km, then turns left and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 156 km west, turns right and walks 285 km, then turns right and walks 4 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: H is the mother of G. B is the daughter of G. E is the father of G. How is B related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. E is a parent of G, and B is G’s daughter. Hence B is E’s grandchild.

questions.stem: F is the brother of B. B is the mother of G. A is the father of F and B. How is F related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. F is the brother of G’s mother B. Therefore F is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: E is the only daughter of F. F is the father of E. C is the son of E. H is the sister of F. How is F related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of E, and E is C’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 36 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 24. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 36 − 13 + 1 = 24.

questions.stem: In a queue of 61 candidates, a candidate is 18th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. New front rank = 18+4 = 22. Back rank = 61 − 22 + 1 = 40.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹3100 each. One earns 20% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 6027.78. Recover each cost separately: 3100×100/120 + 3100×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 42 and 63 hours. An outlet empties it in 126 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 31.5. Net rate = 1/42 + 1/63 − 1/126 = 2/63 tank/hour. Required time = 31.5 hours.

questions.stem: A boat covers 102 km in still water in 6 hours. If the stream flows at 5 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. Still-water speed = 17 km/h. Upstream speed = 17 − 5. Distance = speed × 3.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 9:5. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 6 months. A receives ₹108000 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 138000. Profit ratio is 108:30. Each ratio unit = ₹1000. Total = 138 × 1000.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹12000 earns ₹5400 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15870. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 15%. Compound amount = 12000 × (1 + 15/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 140 litres of pure milk. 28 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 89.6. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 140 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 16 people is 51 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 68. New total minus old total = (16+1)×(51+1) − 16×51 = 68.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 16 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 48. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+16)/(x+16) = 3/2 gives x = 16. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 140 m train moving at 79.2 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 7.37. Relative speed = (79.2 − 10.8) ×5/18 = 19 m/s. Time = 140/19.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹2700. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.
